status: original synthetic classroom inputs, not actual accounts or tax advice
scope: A small market stall buys finished goods for resale. This separate teaching case does not value growing crops, livestock, home-grown harvests or the whole farm. All amounts are invented. No VAT or income-tax calculation is included. Specified carrying values and period costs are supplied exercise assumptions, not accounting policies for a real business.

events.title: Collect an older sale
events.evidence: R200 receipt linked to the opening customer balance. The sale belongs to the earlier period.

events.title: Receive resale stock
events.evidence: Supplier invoice and goods received: R400 carrying cost, R250 paid, R150 still owed. Stock is not yet sold.

events.title: Deliver a credit sale
events.evidence: Delivery and accepted R900 credit invoice establish the sale in this case. Goods supplied have verified carrying cost R350. No payment yet.

events.title: Collect part of that sale
events.evidence: Receipt linked to S01. R600 settles part of R900; it is not a second sale.

events.title: Pay an amount already owed
events.evidence: Supplier statement and payment match R200 of the payable balance. No new expense is created by this settlement.

events.title: Buy a lasting tool
events.evidence: R300 paid. For this exercise, the item qualifies as equipment and is available for use. Its period charge is supplied separately by D01.

events.title: Receive borrowed money
events.evidence: R500 advance and matching obligation. No withheld fee in this case. Borrowing is not a sale.

events.title: Separate repayment from interest
events.evidence: R110 paid: R100 principal and R10 interest for this period. No other charge in this simplified schedule.

events.title: Take money for the household
events.evidence: Owner takes R150 for personal use. This is a withdrawal of equity, not wages or a business expense in this case.

events.title: Include a January service
events.evidence: Signed January transport completion record supports an agreed R80 charge. Invoice arrives 2 February. No payment by 31 January.

events.title: Pay for a future service
events.evidence: R120 paid for storage supplied wholly in February. The unused right is a prepayment at 31 January, under this exercise assumption.

events.title: Pay a January running cost
events.evidence: R60 utility charge relates entirely to January and is paid on 31 January.

events.title: Check what remains in stock
events.evidence: Approved physical count, valuation and reconciliation confirm R300 closing stock and a R50 loss. This is not a guess from an unexplained count difference.

events.title: Include the supplied equipment charge
events.evidence: Reviewed exercise schedule supplies R60 depreciation for January across the equipment. No useful life, rate or tax allowance is inferred.

outsidePeriod.evidence: Remaining S01 balance collected in February. Keep it outside January cash.

missingCase.reason: Closing stock count and valuation are missing. Book stock before review remains R350, but adjusted stock, period profit and complete position are not yet verified.

reviewCards.claim: The app printed a VAT number, so this must be a valid tax invoice.
reviewCards.reason: A field or document title does not prove the relevant registration, supply treatment or required particulars. Use current SARS guidance and an appropriate reviewer.

reviewCards.claim: I did not have to submit a return, so I can discard every source record.
reviewCards.reason: Do not infer record duties from that one fact. Check the applicable requirements and any audit, dispute or other retention obligation before disposal.

reviewCards.claim: This export is a complete set of accounts for a loan application.
reviewCards.reason: Reconcile the export with stock, amounts owed, assets, debt and other source records. A summary does not prove completeness or approval.

reviewCards.claim: A missing stock valuation should be entered as zero so the totals work.
reviewCards.reason: Keep the missing value explicit and request evidence. Balanced arithmetic alone cannot prove correct classification or complete records.
